questions.prompt: What does `readonly` on an interface property guarantee?

options.text: The object is frozen at runtime
The property cannot be reassigned after creation (a compile-time check)

questions.explanation: readonly is a compile-time rule forbidding reassignment. Like all types it is erased, so the runtime object is still a normal mutable object.

questions.prompt: When you read an optional property `email?: string`, what is its type?
questions.explanation: An optional property may be absent, so reading it yields string | undefined; you must handle the missing case.

questions.prompt: When do excess property checks apply?

options.text: Only when assigning a fresh object literal directly to a typed target
Never — TypeScript allows extra properties always

questions.explanation: Excess property checks reject unknown properties on fresh object literals. Assigning through a variable first uses ordinary structural compatibility instead.

questions.prompt: To allow arbitrary string keys with number values, you add an ______ signature like [key: string]: number. (one word)
questions.explanation: An index signature ([key: string]: number) describes open-ended keys of a known value type.

questions.prompt: How do you make one interface include the properties of another?
questions.explanation: Interfaces compose with extends, inheriting the base interface's members.

questions.prompt: Which statements about structural typing are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Any object with the required properties matches the interface
An object must be explicitly declared as the interface type to match
The object's declared name must equal the interface name

questions.explanation: With structural typing, any value whose shape has the required properties matches — no explicit declaration or matching name is needed.
